Real adult proportions: about 1.8 m tall and about 7.5 heads high. Shrink the head from r=0.2 to an ellipsoid about 0.23 m tall. Add a neck cylinder and trapezius slopes. Make the shoulders about 0.42 m wide, wider than the hips. Raise the hips to about 0.95 m so the legs are longer. Shape the torso as a LatheGeometry profile that tapers from chest to waist and is flattened front to back (z about 0.7).

A real joint hierarchy made of nested Groups: pelvis > spine > chest > neck > head; shoulder > upper arm > elbow > forearm > wrist > hand; hip > thigh > knee > shin > ankle > foot (with a heel/toe pivot). Use tapered capsule or Lathe segments, and hide small spheres at the joints so no gaps show when they bend.

Optional step up: merge the segments into one procedural SkinnedMesh with about 15 Bones and skin weights based on distance to each bone. This gives a single continuous body with no visible seams, using only standard Three.js and no external model files.

Readable hands, since hands are now central: a palm box, a thumb capsule and four 2-segment finger capsules. The fingers curl around ledges, bars, rope and zipline handles while holding, spread when falling, and loosely close when running. Shimmying alternates hand over hand.

Two-bone IK. While hanging, both hands snap exactly to the ledge or bar contact points (offset about ±0.2 m) and the elbows bend naturally. On the ground, raycast the feet to the platform so they plant on edges and steps; this matters most on moving platforms and turntables.

A run cycle driven by distance so the feet never slide: phase = distance travelled / stride length (about 2.2 m at 9 m/s). It goes through contact, down, passing and up. Arms counter-swing with the elbows bent about 90 degrees, shoulders counter-rotate against the hips, the pelvis bobs twice per cycle, and the torso leans with acceleration. Blend smoothly between idle, jog and sprint.

Banking and smooth facing: lean into turns in proportion to speed times turn rate, and slerp the facing toward the movement direction instead of snapping. On ice the feet slip and the arms flail; on conveyors the runner staggers slightly.

Jump phases: an 80 ms anticipation crouch, full extension at takeoff, a knee tuck at the apex, legs reaching down before landing, and a landing squash scaled by impact speed. A parkour forward roll plays after drops of more than about 4-5 m at speed. The double jump is a clear front tuck flip.

Hanging and climbing poses:
- A braced hang with the feet against the wall when there is a wall under the ledge; a free hang under bars, with the legs dangling and swinging with pendulum lag after the catch.
- Climbing up is a mantle sequence: chest to the edge, elbow up, knee on the edge, stand.
- When grip is below 25-30% the arms tremble and the fingers slip, so grip stamina shows on the body even without the HUD.
Chalk is shown on the hands only. Using it whitens the palms and fingers and puffs white dust particles when you grab or clap. A chalk bag hangs on the belt once chalk is owned.

Visible equipment that matches the shop: fingerless gloves when Klatrehandsker are owned, a chalk bag on the hip, and a coiled rope over the shoulder once the rope is bought. On the skate level, add a helmet and knee pads.

Rope pose: one hand above the other on the rope, the legs together and trailing the swing, the body lined up with the rope, and the arms opening for balance on release. Zipline and trapeze use a two-handed overhead hang with the legs tucked.

Skateboard pose: sideways stance with the knees bent and the arms out for balance, leaning into turns, pushing with the back foot when W is pressed, an ollie sequence (crouch, pop, knees up, extend), a low crouch on grind rails, and an automatic indy grab on big airs.

Face and head: white sclera with dark irises, eyelids that blink every 3-6 s, brows, a small nose and ears, and short hair built from a few clumped, slightly noisy spheres. The head turns toward the next ledge or anchor, or the camera's aim, and looks down when standing near an edge.

Clothing and materials:
- Hoodie with a hood (a half torus), drawstrings, a kangaroo pocket and cuffs; joggers with ankle cuffs.
- Sneakers made from an extruded sneaker outline with a white midsole and a lace stripe.
- Fabric uses MeshPhysicalMaterial with sheen and a CanvasTexture noise normal map. Skin is warm-toned with low roughness and a slight sheen for a soft look.
- Roughness varies by material: shoes glossier, fabric matte.
Secondary motion with simple spring-dampers on the hood, drawstrings, hair tufts, the hoodie hem, the chalk bag and the rope coil. They flap during falls and swings and settle when standing still.

Idle life and weight: breathing (the chest scales by about 1.5%), shifting weight between the feet, glancing around, catching breath with heaving shoulders after long hangs, clapping chalk off the hands, dust puffs on footsteps and a dust ring on landing.

Readability: a soft contact blob shadow under the feet together with the real cast shadow, so landings are easier to judge, plus a subtle fresnel rim light so the figure stands out against both the bright dawn skies and the dark storm and space skies.
